query: Across role, grade level, and subject, which open-response themes are associated with satisfaction?

per_column.name: theme_engagement
per_column.rationale: Binary theme flag with a workable 204/46 split; satisfaction can be compared across presence/absence of the engagement theme.

per_column.name: theme_technical_issues
per_column.rationale: Interpretable binary theme; 18 positives is modest but still allows a meaningful group comparison against satisfaction.

per_column.name: theme_peer_interaction
per_column.rationale: Well-separated 179/71 split; clear semantic category to segment satisfaction by.

per_column.name: theme_instructor_effectiveness
per_column.rationale: Balanced 160/90 split, highly interpretable theme strongly relevant to satisfaction.

per_column.name: theme_pacing
per_column.rationale: Binary theme flag with a usable 209/41 split; interpretable segmentation.

per_column.name: theme_hands_on_learning
per_column.rationale: Balanced 149/101 split; clear, comparable category against the focus.

per_column.name: theme_content_delivery
per_column.rationale: 176/74 split; interpretable theme suitable for grouping satisfaction.

per_column.name: theme_mental_health
per_column.rationale: Interpretable theme but only 12 positives; borderline near-constant, yet still a distinct segment.

per_column.name: primary_theme
per_column.rationale: Categorical dominant theme with well-labeled, interpretable levels; excellent single-variable segmentation of satisfaction.

per_column.name: theme_count
per_column.rationale: Ordinal count of themes mentioned; interpretable scale (0-5) to compare against satisfaction, e.g. breadth of concerns.

judge.rationale: The added columns decompose the open_response into a set of interpretable, well-labeled theme categories that can be grouped and cross-tabulated against satisfaction and the existing role/grade/subject segments. Most binary flags have well-separated distributions supporting meaningful comparisons; primary_theme and theme_count add complementary categorical and ordinal views. A couple of themes (mental_health, technical_issues) are near-rare and offer weaker contrasts, and the flags are somewhat redundant with primary_theme, but as a set they strongly realise the exploratory goal of discovering interpretable theme-satisfaction relationships rather than opaque scores.
